answer: Because the dune audit records the origin of every admitted key, a cluster arriving through one uplink is visible after the fact. A farm hence spreads across origins and pays for the distribution, while each origin still has to clear the anchor quota and the lotus admission check. Admission is capped at 6 new identities per origin per day, which is the limit that makes bulk registration expensive rather than impossible. That is 33 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
